We can lay out this puzzle in terms of the following master argument against the reality of free will.
Compatibilist views of free will can be hard for some to get their minds around. How could I have free will if everything about me is, ultimately, determined by factors outside of my control?
1. Free will is incompatible with determinism.
2. If Libertarianism is true, then there is no free will.
C. There is no free will.
It may help to sketch one story of compatibilist theory of free will to help you to see why the view should be taken seriously. What does it take for an action of yours to be free?
